unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The first reconstructed component is “System frame: 2026-07-28-eval-174737 · rag-ingestion-retrieval,” described as naming the depicted system/evaluation.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief provides no date-stamped evaluation identifier or formal system name. This is extraneous board metadata rather than a supported architectural claim.

verdict.strongest_transmitted_behavior: The version-consistent publication and embedding-generation rebuild stories are transmitted most strongly: three retrieval stores are gated on a common version, partial publication is unavailable and repaired or rolled back, and a background rebuild remains off the live path until complete, consistent, atomic promotion with rollback retention.
verdict.most_consequential_loss: Failure recovery is incomplete: the reconstruction does not communicate that one unparseable document leaves the rest of its batch running, does not make exhausted persistent failures the explicit dead-letter trigger, and omits reprocessing from the dead-letter store.
verdict.overall_summary: The reconstruction preserves the complete system shape and the primary ingestion-to-grounded-answer path, including ACL propagation, hash-based version handling, overlapping metadata-bearing chunks, rate-limited embedding, synchronized publication, parallel hybrid retrieval, reranking, permission filtering, citations, feedback, and safe index-generation switchover. No system-defining flow is contradicted. Fidelity falls short of fully actionable implementation detail because several operational semantics are softened or absent: concrete source classes, per-document batch isolation, dead-letter exhaustion and reprocessing, an explicit generation-service boundary and retrieved-evidence-only rule, exact low-confidence triggers, and a visibly closed feedback loop. The result is highly usable for design discussion, but a few failure and degraded-mode details still require clarification.
